blocks.body: Present Perfect: Questions and Short Answers — Have you...?, What have you...?, How long have you...?, Yes, I have. / No, he hasn't.

{"level":"A2–B1","intro":"In Present Perfect Yes/No questions, put have / has before the subject and use the main verb in V3. In a Wh-question, add the question word before have / has.","rules":[{"label":"Have I / you / we / they ...?","color":"emerald","text":"With these subjects, start a Yes/No question with have.","example":"Have you finished the task?"},{"label":"Has he / she / it ...?","color":"blue","text":"With he / she / it, use has.","example":"Has she called you?"},{"label":"Wh-word + have / has + subject + V3?","color":"violet","text":"Put what, where, why, how long, or how many before have / has.","example":"What have you done? / How long has she lived here?"},{"label":"Short answers","color":"amber","text":"Repeat have / has or haven't / hasn't. Do not contract an affirmative short answer: Yes, she has, not Yes, she's.","example":"Yes, I have. / No, he hasn't."}]}

{"title":"1. Basic question patterns","intro":"In a Yes/No question, have / has comes before the subject; in a Wh-question, put the question word before it.","items":[{"label":"I / you / we / they","title":"Have + subject + V3?","subtitle":"Have you seen this film? / Have they arrived?"},{"label":"he / she / it","title":"Has + subject + V3?","subtitle":"Has he finished? / Has it started?"},{"label":"Wh-questions","title":"Wh-word + have / has + subject + V3?","subtitle":"Where has she gone? / How many books have you read?"},{"label":"Short answers","title":"Yes, ... have / has. / No, ... haven't / hasn't.","subtitle":"Has Anna arrived? — Yes, she has. Match the pronoun and do not write Yes, she's."}]}

{"title":"2. Questions we ask","sections":[{"label":"About experience","color":"emerald","description":"Ask about experience up to now, often with ever. Ever goes between the subject and V3.","examples":[{"en":"Have you ever been to Italy?","ua":"Experience up to now."},{"en":"Has she ever tried sushi?","ua":"Life experience without a finished past-time expression."}]},{"label":"About a result by now","color":"blue","description":"Ask whether an action is complete and its result matters now. Already normally goes before V3; yet goes at the end of the question.","examples":[{"en":"Have you finished your homework yet?","ua":"A result up to now."},{"en":"Has he already sent the email?","ua":"The result matters now."}]},{"label":"Wh-questions for details","color":"violet","description":"Put the question word before have / has: question word + have / has + subject + V3. If who is the subject, there is no second subject.","examples":[{"en":"What have you done? / Where has she gone?","ua":"They ask for specific information."},{"en":"Who has called?","ua":"Who is the subject here."}]},{"label":"How long: duration up to now","color":"amber","description":"With states, use How long + Present Perfect and for / since. Present Perfect Continuous is often more natural for an ongoing activity.","examples":[{"en":"How long have you known Anna?","ua":"A state that continues now."},{"en":"How long have you been waiting?","ua":"An ongoing activity."}]},{"label":"Present Perfect or Past Simple?","color":"rose","description":"Present Perfect asks about a current result or experience up to now. Use Past Simple when asking when a completed past event happened or when the question includes a finished-time expression.","examples":[{"en":"Have you sent it yet?","ua":"Is there a result now?"},{"en":"When did you send it?","ua":"When exactly did it happen?"}]}]}

{"title":"3. Questions, details, and short answers","intro":"In a short answer, repeat have / has; a Wh-question needs a content answer.","rows":[{"en":"Have you done the shopping?","ua":"Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.","note":"have → have / haven't"},{"en":"Has Anna called?","ua":"Yes, she has. / No, she hasn't.","note":"Anna → she; has → has / hasn't"},{"en":"What have you done? / Where has she gone?","ua":"Wh-word + have / has + subject + V3","note":"questions for details"},{"en":"Who has called?","ua":"Who + has + V3","note":"who is the subject"},{"en":"Have you sent it yet? / When did you send it?","ua":"result up to now / a specific past time","note":"Present Perfect / Past Simple"}],"warning":"Use V3 after have / has: Has she gone home? Do not contract an affirmative short answer: Yes, she has, not Yes, she's."}

{"title":"4. Common mistakes","items":[{"label":"Mistake 1","color":"rose","title":"Not using inversion in a neutral Yes/No question.","wrong":"❌ She has finished?","right":"✅ Has she finished? The non-inverted order is possible only as an echo question with suitable intonation."},{"label":"Mistake 2","color":"amber","title":"Using the wrong auxiliary form.","wrong":"❌ Have he done it?","right":"✅ Has he done it?"},{"label":"Mistake 3","color":"sky","title":"Using V2 instead of V3.","wrong":"❌ Has she went home?","right":"✅ Has she gone home?"},{"label":"Mistake 4","color":"violet","title":"Contracting an affirmative short answer.","wrong":"❌ Yes, she's.","right":"✅ Yes, she has."},{"label":"Mistake 5","color":"emerald","title":"Using Present Perfect to ask when a completed past event happened.","wrong":"❌ When have you sent the email?","right":"✅ When did you send the email?"}]}

{"title":"5. Short summary","items":["A Yes/No question = Have / Has + subject + V3?","A Wh-question = question word + have / has + subject + V3?; in Who has called?, who is the subject.","Use have with I / you / we / they and has with he / she / it.","In short answers, repeat have / has or haven't / hasn't; do not contract affirmative forms: Yes, she has.","Ever / already normally go between the subject and V3; yet normally goes at the end.","Use How long + Present Perfect with a continuing state; Present Perfect Continuous is often more natural for an activity.","Use Past Simple when asking when a completed event happened and with finished-time expressions such as yesterday or in 2024."]}

{"title":"6. Practice","select_title":"Exercise 1. Choose the correct question","select_intro":"Check have / has, V3, and the contrast with Past Simple.","selects":[{"label":"a) Has she finished the report? / b) Have she finished the report?","prompt":"Which option is correct?","answer":"a"},{"label":"a) When have you sent the email? / b) When did you send the email?","prompt":"We are asking when a completed past action happened.","answer":"b"}],"options":["a","b"],"input_title":"Exercise 2. Build the question","input_intro":"Put the words in the correct order.","inputs":[{"before":"ever / you / have / been / to Canada","after":"→","answer":"Have you ever been to Canada?"},{"before":"How long / she / has / lived / here","after":"→","answer":"How long has she lived here?"}]}
